`specs/minds-eval-harbor/harness_arms.md` covers codex: the `openai` lane is one of the lanes a minds_evals run can sign a workspace in on, and it is no longer listed out of scope. The lane table, the key-variable derivation, the catalog-id notes and the run examples name it, and the observed-model confirmation is documented as picking its naming rule by lane, with a codex id resolving to itself.

The "Codex" follow-up now names what actually remains, and whose it is: mngr's codex transcript emitter writes no per-step `model_name`, which is what leaves a codex trial's observed models empty, while the workspace's own chat app reports no token count for a codex turn, which is what leaves such a trial's usage at zero tokens and an unknown cost. A metering proxy for the lane is still its own follow-up.

The spec now says what a metering proxy on the lane would be worth, and where a proxied codex lane's base URL goes. Such a proxy would close a codex trial's cost gap on its own, and close it wider than the workspace's per-turn token counts can, since it prices every request the workspace makes; it would take over most of the model gap as well, because a proxied trial's confirmation is computed from the proxy's own per-model rows, and only the split between the greeting's model and the arm's still needs a per-step `model_name`. The base URL goes in codex's top-level `openai_base_url` config key, which overrides the built-in openai provider and keeps auth on `auth.json` -- not in `model_providers`, which cannot override a built-in provider and would authenticate from an env var instead of the account (verified against codex 0.147.0).

The spec's grading section no longer calls the harness report's shell-level failure signatures harness-blind without qualification: they are harness-blind in what they match, but nothing on a codex trajectory reaches them, because the scan reads shell output by tool name and knows only claude's and pi's spellings. The same list is what puts command output into the transcript the `quality` judges read, so a codex cell's quality score is read on a conversation without it -- and the spec now says which way that bends the score: the progress timeline comes from the same output, an absent timeline is scored 10 by rule, and `quality` is an equal-weight mean of five criteria, so a codex trial banks one free full mark in five. The `progress_timeline_was_read` gate that would otherwise catch a renderer reading nothing is inert there for the same reason.
